name: Oral defense / Viva voce
dinh_nghia: Oral defense (viva voce, Latin: 'living voice') is an assessment method in which a student must verbally explain, justify, and defend their work before an examiner or panel. In the context of academic integrity, it serves as an authentication mechanism: a student who did not actually engage with the work they submitted cannot convincingly explain it under direct questioning. The 'spot viva' model — randomly sampling a subset of written submissions for a 15–20 minute oral follow-up — applies this principle at scale without requiring all students to undergo a full oral examination.
phan_loai: Prevention method against multiple forms of academic dishonesty: (1) AI-assisted dishonesty — student cannot explain content generated by an LLM; (2) contract cheating — student cannot explain work produced by a third party; (3) collusion — individual oral questioning reveals whether the student has genuine understanding of 'group' contributions. Unlike detection tools that analyze text artifacts, oral defense authenticates the person rather than the product.
lich_su_khai_niem: Oral examination is among the oldest forms of academic assessment, predating written examinations in universities. The viva voce for PhD theses has been standard practice in UK and Australian universities for over a century. The 'spot viva' as a scalable anti-cheating mechanism for undergraduate coursework gained renewed attention after ChatGPT's release (November 2022), with prominent advocacy in Times Higher Education (2023) and The Conversation (2023). University of Western Ontario implemented oral exams for a 600-student undergraduate business class as early as 2023–2024.
ten_truong_hop: Spot viva implementations at University of Sydney (Australia), UC San Diego (USA), and University of Western Ontario (Canada), 2023–2025. Macquarie University Law School (Australia) adopted viva voce assessment for undergraduate law students, explicitly citing academic integrity and employability goals.
dien_bien: Following the mass adoption of generative AI tools in 2022–2023, universities worldwide faced an authentication crisis: written submissions could not reliably be attributed to students. University of Western Ontario implemented oral exams for an undergraduate business cohort of approximately 600 students. University of Sydney updated its Academic Integrity Policy (2023) to treat unapproved AI use as a breach, and oral assessment is one recommended verification mechanism. UC San Diego's Academic Integrity Office, led by director Tricia Bertram Gallant, acknowledged that ensuring students do not use AI is 'challenging' if they are not completing work in front of an assessor. Times Higher Education published an opinion piece (2023) by academics advocating sampled vivas as a scalable, cost-effective solution for large cohorts.
ket_qua_xu_ly: No punishment case per se — oral defense is a preventive design, not an investigation tool. When implemented as spot viva: students who engaged genuinely with their work pass without difficulty; students who submitted AI-generated or third-party work typically cannot explain methodological choices, sources, or reasoning, which results in grade revision or academic misconduct referral. Macquarie Law School reports improved student engagement and employability outcomes alongside integrity benefits.
con_so_thong_ke: University of Western Ontario: 600 students in one undergraduate business class assessed via oral exams (2023–2024). Times Higher Education (2023): UK universities already retain viva option for investigating suspected written assessment misconduct — estimated hundreds of spot vivas conducted annually. No comprehensive cross-institutional dataset on spot viva adoption rates exists as of 2025. [uncertain]
hai_cho_nguoi_hoc: Oral defense is generally beneficial for learners who engage authentically: it develops communication skills, metacognitive reflection, and discipline-specific discourse — all valued in professional contexts. The harm is asymmetric: students with social anxiety, speech disabilities, or non-native speaker disadvantage may perform below their actual knowledge level. Students with autism spectrum conditions or selective mutism face accessibility barriers. These concerns are well-documented in assessment literature and require reasonable accommodations.
hai_cho_nghien_cuu: Oral defense is an integrity mechanism, not itself a source of harm to knowledge. However, if spot vivas are conducted inconsistently or with poorly trained examiners, they may produce unreliable assessments, creating false negatives (missing genuine misconduct) or false positives (penalizing anxious but honest students). The research gap is the lack of large-scale empirical studies on spot viva effectiveness and fairness across student demographics.
hai_cho_xa_hoi: Widespread adoption of spot vivas, if implemented fairly, would restore confidence in the authenticity of academic credentials — directly counteracting the credentialing crisis created by AI-assisted cheating. The cost barrier (examiner time, scheduling) may entrench quality gaps between well-resourced and under-resourced institutions, potentially widening inequality.
cong_cu_phat_hien: Oral defense is itself the detection mechanism — no software tool involved. The examiner functions as the detector by probing understanding through targeted questions. Unlike automated tools (Turnitin AI, GPTZero), oral defense has no false positive rate when the examiner is competent: a student who understands their work will demonstrate it. The limitation is examiner skill and bias rather than algorithmic error.
han_che_cong_cu: Cost and scalability are the primary constraints: a 15–20 minute spot viva requires significant faculty time. For a course of 300 students with 10% random sampling, this is approximately 10 hours of examiner time per assessment cycle. Accessibility challenges for students with speech/communication disabilities require accommodation planning. Cross-cultural communication differences may disadvantage international students. Examiner bias (accent, presentation style) can introduce unfairness not present in written assessment.
watermarking: Oral defense and LLM watermarking address complementary aspects of the same problem. Watermarking (Kirchenbauer/UMD, Aaronson/OpenAI) embeds detectable statistical signals in AI-generated text, enabling post-hoc detection in written submissions. Oral defense prevents the problem upstream by requiring students to authenticate their understanding in real time. If watermarking matures, it may reduce the need for resource-intensive oral assessment; conversely, oral defense remains robust even against watermark-stripping techniques.
thiet_ke_bai_tap: The spot viva model: (1) Students submit written work as normal; (2) A random 10–20% sample is selected after submission; (3) Selected students attend a 15–20 minute oral follow-up with examiner; (4) Examiner asks questions drawn directly from the submitted work — methodology, sources, reasoning, implications; (5) Oral performance is integrated into the final grade. Variants: process-based submission (Google Docs history, draft progression) combined with spot viva for flagged cases. University of Sydney recommends oral components for high-stakes assessments. Macquarie Law School uses structured viva rubrics for formative and summative assessment.
chinh_sach_truong_hoc: University of Sydney (2023 Academic Integrity Policy): unapproved AI use is a breach; oral assessment recommended as verification. UC San Diego: Academic Integrity Office acknowledges limitations of text-based detection; promotes authentic assessment including oral components. University of Western Ontario: implemented oral exams at scale for large undergraduate cohorts. Macquarie University: formal viva voce assessment in law faculty with published teaching resources (TECHE, 2023). UK universities: many retain viva option in regulations for investigating suspected written assessment misconduct.
van_hoa_to_chuc: Oral defense aligns with McCabe's honor code culture approach: it shifts the assessment environment toward demonstrated understanding rather than punitive surveillance. Students who know a spot viva is possible are incentivized to genuinely engage with assigned material — changing behavior at the assignment design level rather than relying on detection after-the-fact. This is consistent with McCabe's finding that honor-code cultures outperform enforcement-only cultures in long-term integrity outcomes.
ai_literacy: Implementing spot vivas is itself a form of AI literacy intervention: by requiring students to articulate their reasoning, educators signal that AI tools cannot substitute for genuine understanding. Faculty training for oral assessment (question design, bias mitigation, accessibility accommodations) constitutes an important form of educator AI literacy. ISTE frameworks support authentic assessment practices that measure critical thinking, which oral defense inherently does.
khung_quoc_te: UNESCO 2023 guidance on AI in education recommends 'assessment redesign' as a primary institutional response to AI-assisted cheating — oral defense is explicitly consistent with this recommendation. EU AI Act (2024) Annex III classifies AI systems used in 'education and vocational training' as high-risk where they determine access or outcomes; oral defense as human-administered assessment is not affected by AI Act restrictions.
phap_luat_viet_nam: Vietnam's Nghị định 109/2022/NĐ-CP (Điều 20) establishes academic integrity requirements for scientific activities but does not specify assessment modalities. Oral defense (vấn đáp) is standard in Vietnamese higher education for thesis defense and some professional examinations, but is rarely applied as a routine anti-cheating mechanism for coursework. No Vietnamese regulatory framework specifically mandates or encourages spot vivas. The assessment remains at institutional discretion.
chinh_sach_chau_a: NUS (Singapore) has piloted oral assessment components for coursework in selected faculties following its 2023/2024 disclosure framework update. CUHK (Hong Kong) primarily uses detection and disciplinary response rather than preventive oral assessment. No comprehensive pan-Asian data on spot viva adoption exists as of 2025. [uncertain]
ai_tutor_vs_ai_cheater: Oral defense directly resolves the Rose Luckin (UCL) / Neil Selwyn (Monash) debate at the assessment level: it is agnostic to how students used AI tools during learning, and evaluates only whether genuine understanding was achieved. A student who used AI as a tutor (Luckin's positive framing) will be able to demonstrate knowledge; a student who used AI to produce work without engagement (Selwyn's concern) will not. This makes oral defense uniquely suited as an integration-friendly assessment: it accommodates AI-assisted learning while preventing AI-substituted learning.
edtech_company_policies: EdTech platforms have begun integrating oral/viva elements: Coursera's 'AI-based Viva Exam' (June 2024) generates follow-up questions from submitted written work — a digital analogue of the spot viva. Oral defense in traditional settings requires no EdTech infrastructure. The Duolingo English Test uses human-in-the-loop proctoring for spoken components. Khan Academy's Khanmigo uses Socratic dialogue — philosophically adjacent to the oral defense principle of requiring students to explain their reasoning.
de_xuat_nha_nghien_cuu: From an EdTech researcher perspective: (1) Spot viva should be adopted as standard practice for high-stakes coursework — random sampling at 10–20% makes it cost-effective; (2) Institutions should develop clear rubrics, training for examiners, and accessibility accommodation protocols before rollout; (3) Oral defense should be presented to students as a learning opportunity, not a surveillance mechanism — framing matters for trust; (4) Research priority: large-scale empirical studies on spot viva effectiveness, fairness across student demographics, and optimal sampling rates; (5) Combination design: written submission + process evidence (draft history) + spot viva creates a layered authentication system more robust than any single method.

nguon_viet_nam: Oral defense (vấn đáp/bảo vệ khóa luận) is institutionalized in Vietnamese higher education for thesis work under MOET regulations. No specific Vietnamese source on spot viva as an AI-cheating prevention mechanism for coursework. The approach is highly relevant to Vietnamese context given rising AI use among students (Nghiên cứu Springer 2024: 1,386 sinh viên Việt Nam sample). Institutional adoption would require adaptation of current assessment norms.
